gap: No result ChatGPT got states a US price for either of its two carded picks, and none states that ANNKE's own US store sells the DR85, an 8-BNC CVBS/AHD/TVI/CVI DVR with human and vehicle detection, for $79.99 on 2026-11-17. ChatGPT's 'best value' ANNKE 8-channel AI DVR card was $234.99 at Newegg.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages (dahuasecurity.com XVR7208A-4K-I3 and securitylab.hikvision.com DS-7208HQHI-S1/XT) and the other top results (Dahua datasheet PDFs for XVR7108HE-4K-I3 and XVR5108HS-5M-I3, the Dahua HDCVI selection catalog, the Hikvision iDS datasheet, and two B&H Dahua listings). The maker pages and PDFs list no prices. The B&H pages were in the results, but B&H blocked my fetch, so I could not check them. No result ChatGPT got gives a maker-store price for an 8-channel 5-in-1 DVR with detection under $100. It also never gave a price or US retailer for its two picks, and my search found no US seller with a USD price for the XVR7208A-4K-I3.
decides: For a homeowner keeping 8 analog cameras, the price-sourced pick is the ANNKE DR85 at $79.99. It takes all four coax formats including old CVBS and has human and vehicle detection on the maker's own US store. That costs about a third of ChatGPT's $234.99 Newegg ANNKE card. Step up to the DR168 ($279.99, 16 channels, analog up to 8MP) only if the cameras are 4K TVI. The Viewtron VT-DVR-8 ($799.99) is only worth it if an NDAA-compliant DVR is required. ChatGPT's Dahua and Hikvision picks have no US maker store and no US price I could source today. The one US Hikvision listing I opened is out of stock and sold as-is with no warranty.

findings.label: FCC rules on Hikvision/Dahua for home buyers
findings.value: Use-based: covers Hikvision, Dahua and Hytera telecom and video-surveillance equipment used 'for the purpose of public safety, security of government facilities'; the Second Report and Order blocks 'further importation and marketing of already authorized covered equipment while allowing continued use'
findings.source_title: FCC 26-50, Protecting Against National Security Threats to the Communications Supply Chain through the Equipment Authorization Program, Third Report and Order (adopted 2026-07-22)
findings.note: I read only the first 100k of 410k characters. The visible paragraphs (5, 7) do not name Hikvision or Dahua in the import/marketing ban. ChatGPT already warned about 'U.S. regulatory restrictions', so this is not the gap.
